concepts.name: 01-flat-crest
concepts.title: Flat crest
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Task: Create a close logo variation from the supplied reference board for "Flight Deck". Reference image 1 is the source for the SYMBOL GEOMETRY, especially the large dark symbol in the bottom-right panel. Recompose as a clean standalone logo on white; do not recreate the board or its photography.
Stay close to this specific design language: a flat almost horizontal top, a short 45-degree chamfered left shoulder, a short horizontal underside ledge on the left that turns through a small rounded inside elbow into a short downward-pointing stem, and a broad curved winglike upper wedge extending to the upper right. Below it is a SEPARATE curved blade with a sharp descending lower-left tip and a sharp upper-right tip. A narrow continuous white swept channel separates the two dark pieces. The lower blade and upper wedge have generous curved bellies. It should have the same compact forward/upward momentum as the reference.
Critical geometry: exactly two solid pieces. Straight upper roof and angled shoulder are essential. Keep the short left underside ledge and recessed inner elbow visible. Do not replace the upper-left shoulder with a large round C-shaped curve. The lower blade is detached, no connecting left spine. No ring or orbit.
Presentation: square pure white canvas. One large flat near-black #0B0F18 logo symbol centered in the upper middle, around 58 percent canvas width. Below it place the exact text "Flight Deck", centered, medium-weight modern sans serif, text about 48 percent canvas width, with ample separation and margins. No other text, no "Find", no TM. Clean crisp vector-like raster concept.
Avoid: photography, mountain scenes, gradients, shadows, texture, 3D, outlines, duplicate marks, logo grids, labels, circles, birds, feathers, actual airplanes. Focus on the two shapes and their shared white channel.

Variation: FLAT CREST. This is the closest baseline to the reference. Width to height about 1.45:1. Keep a long truly level roof, a restrained rounded transition into the diagonal left shoulder, the distinct recessed elbow below, and a broad detached lower blade. The white channel curves steeply upward from the lower left and becomes a shallow rising sweep near the right tip. Give the upper wedge slightly more weight and the lower blade a slightly shorter downward reach than the reference. Four sharp terminals, controlled curves, no additional cuts.
